findings.claim: The briefing is to name the `audit` skill, but main has no audit skill. plugin/skills/ on main holds only continue, handoff and write-docs. `audit` (plus architecture-review, decision-log-review and practices-review) lives in the audit-agent-and-skills ticket, which is still in building and is not in this plan's depends_on. If this ticket lands first, the briefing sends every session to a skill that does not exist (ADR 0002 routing becomes wrong in a new way). The 'four kmctl skills' count and the test 'fails when a kmctl skill is not named' also have no fixed meaning: a hard-coded list of four goes stale, and a list read from plugin/skills/ has three skills today and seven after audit-agent-and-skills lands. The Intent also cites plugin/skills/audit/evals/, which is not on main. Fix: add audit-agent-and-skills to depends_on (or drop `audit` from the list), and say which skills the briefing names and where the test gets that list.

The audit skill was not on main and its ticket was not a dependency; the briefing test had no fixed list. The revised plan lists audit-agent-and-skills in depends_on and reads skill names from the packaged plugin's skills/ folder at run time, so the test checks every folder there.

Two new Consequences overstate the code. 0005 says the action fails only when kmctl check fails, but action/knowledge-ci.sh also exits 1 when kmctl review due crashes (its own header says so), and audit mode exits 1 when claude errors or gives no findings. 0006 says every concept an agent writes is due until a person verifies it, but review_due skips handoffs (review_due.py:161), so handoffs are never due as unverified.

The 12-word cut leaves punctuation before the ellipsis ('handoff: ... so you,...') and gives the three review skills the same cut-off line ('The review instructions for .okf/X/ pages, used by the audit skill and...'), which never says to use them through /audit. Strip trailing punctuation before adding '...'.

src/kmctl/briefing.py has an unstaged ruff format change. The stamp ran on the working tree, which is formatted; the staged copy fails ruff format --check (checked on a copy). Stage it so what lands is what was stamped.
